title: a birthplace the rule keeps once its words are answered
line: the Massachusetts birth register's Northampton, the record of the birth itself, against the 1940 census's Pennsylvania, secondary information an informant gave: the classes favour the register without doubt, but a place is kept only as a place, so the rule waits on the owner's answer to the register's words and says so; the owner's answer to the words lets the rule go over the conflicts there and then, and its own answer says the rule resolved the birthplace for Northampton, the event's place the register's, the census's Pennsylvania staying as the census says it; reconsider keeps it, and the written conclusion prints the resolution with its reason
